idiom_name: recursive generic bound (class Base<T extends Base<T>>) for self-typed APIs
implementation_notes: Java's analogue of the CRTP base is the recursive (F-bounded) type parameter: abstract class Builder<T extends Builder<T>> with an abstract accessor returning T; java.lang.Enum<E extends Enum<E>> is the JDK's own use of the shape, guaranteeing that compareTo takes the concrete enum type. The JVM still dispatches instance methods virtually and generics are erased, so this idiom buys compile-time self-typing and shared base behaviour (fluent builders, mutually comparable value classes, enum-like hierarchies) rather than vtable-free calls; use it when the derived type must appear in signatures or return types, and prefer sealed interfaces plus exhaustive pattern matching where the hierarchy is closed and new operations, not new types, are expected.
pitfalls: The recursive bound is not self-enforcing: class Apple extends Builder<Orange> compiles whenever Orange extends Builder<Orange>, so self() and compareTo then deal in the wrong type; only discipline or a runtime check prevents it.

Writing the accessor as (T) this is an unchecked cast over erased generics that can throw ClassCastException at runtime; declaring an abstract self() and returning this in the subclass keeps the cast out of the base.
Generics are erased, so static members cannot use the class's type parameter: the per-type counter or registry use of CRTP needs a Class-keyed map or a per-subclass constant instead.
